requirements.requirement: Root crontab on node1 runs /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 with output retained in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
requirements.summary: crontab -l shows '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' installed immediately after configuration (cmd-1672b55f18a14c09) and confirmed present after a full reboot (cmd-dfb0a37230fd4237), matching the required schedule and log path exactly.

requirements.requirement: The inventory-maintenance script executes successfully and its real output is captured in the retention log
requirements.summary: The prepared script contained leaked heredoc artifacts (a literal trailing 'SCRIPT' line and chown/chmod commands appended to the script body) causing a runtime error 'SCRIPT: command not found' on the first manual run (cmd-1672b55f18a14c09). The executor rewrote the script to a clean, working version (cmd-07be338e53c5477f) and confirmed it appends correct timestamped output both before and after reboot (cmd-2eeb90be1b73447d, cmd-dfb0a37230fd4237). This was a necessary correction to a pre-existing defect rather than scope creep, since the task requires the script's output to actually be captured.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered cron/script/log/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline captured boot_id 513c865e-e121-4025-a0a4-8689cc580398 with active crond, installed crontab, and log content (cmd-2eeb90be1b73447d), consistent with the fixed after-prepare snapshot. A backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned an acknowledgement before disconnect (cmd-5bb1e60c5c0c4d50), the connection then timed out (cmd-5f1c11d6127f4b6d) and reconnected (cmd-1923dd241b5c40fa). Post-restart checks show a new boot_id 9784a039-8815-4e02-a3f2-1a0352bf1af1, active crond, intact crontab, intact/executable script, preserved log content, and a fresh manual run appending correctly (cmd-dfb0a37230fd4237). This matches the fixed after-executor snapshot boot-identity exactly, providing a full pre/disruption/post transition.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material outcomes: a correctly scheduled crontab entry (15 2 * * *) that pipes the maintenance script's output into /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log, a working script (after fixing a pre-existing heredoc-corruption defect in the prepared file) that produces real captured output, and a complete, well-evidenced restart cycle on node1 showing baseline health, acknowledged reboot, changed boot identity, and full recovery of cron, script, and log state, cross-confirmed by the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: The prepared script's SHA-256 hash in the baseline does not match the final script content, since the executor rewrote it to fix a corruption present at prepare time; this is treated as a necessary correction rather than an unauthorized deviation, but is worth noting for anyone comparing against the raw baseline hash.

No evidence of an actual 02:15 cron firing was captured (only manual runs), since the evaluation window did not span a real scheduled trigger; this is inherent to the observation window rather than an executor gap.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: installing the crontab/log (cmd-1672b55f18a14c09) is directly required; rewriting the corrupted script and clearing the stale empty log before re-testing (cmd-07be338e53c5477f) was a necessary fix to a pre-existing defect, not an unnecessary mutation, and the removed log was empty at the time; the reboot (cmd-5bb1e60c5c0c4d50) is required by the fixed restart-evidence protocol. Diagnostic commands (cmd-43ad921236b64877, cmd-7aac0cf364f548fe, cmd-2eeb90be1b73447d, cmd-1923dd241b5c40fa) were read-only. The only incidental residue is /tmp/reboot.log created by the backgrounded shutdown command, a minor, expected byproduct of the reboot mechanism rather than an unrelated mutation, and it did not affect any managed service or security posture. No failed/conflicting services, no unsafe exposure, and no damaged package state appear in the before/after comparisons aside from expected ephemeral PID/systemd-private directory changes from the reboot itself.
